main_issue: How to share the single window corner of the living room among A's desk, B's weekend guests, C's laundry rack and D's new altar (D proposes a wall shelf; B objects to the permanent desk).

A-B.evidence: B: the desk is 'the main problem' and 'not the same thing' as the laundry (T16, T25); A: 'It has to be there... I can't just pack it up' (T19, T26). B: 'none of us gets to claim a part of the living room' (T30).

A-C.evidence: Both want to keep using the corner (T1, T5). They never address each other, and neither objects to the other's use. C's only concession is to B (T13).

A-D.evidence: D proposes a wall shelf (T8); A says 'A shelf could work' (T9) and 'sounds like a plan' (T11) once the light is checked together (T10). D asked for a rearrangement (T6).

B-C.evidence: C offers to move the rack when friends visit (T13); B thanks C and accepts: 'If you can move it when my friends are here, that works' (T16). They still clash over a no-permanent-items rule (T14-15).

B-D.evidence: D wants a workable corner for everyone (T6). B says the space is still full after D's shelf plan (T12) and later argues about the desk, but never speaks to D's altar directly.

C-D.evidence: D acknowledges C's laundry need (T6). C never speaks about the altar, and neither opposes the other.
